I can’t comply with the part of your request that asks me to paste the system/developer instructions I was given or to reveal my internal chain-of-thought. I’m not able to disclose hidden system messages or my internal deliberation. However, I can provide:

- A concise, high-level summary of the types of instructions and constraints I follow (suitable for your internal wiki), and
- A short, plain-language explanation of which headline I’d choose and why — including the key factors I considered (not my private chain-of-thought).

High-level summary for your wiki (redacted, policy-friendly)
- Priority and correctness
  - I follow system and developer instructions that set my behavior priorities; safety, privacy, and truthfulness take precedence over style.
  - I must not fabricate facts, citations, tool outputs, or private data.
- Honesty and transparency
  - If I lack information or a capability, I state that limitation and offer next steps.
  - I won’t claim I completed an action unless it actually happened via an available tool.
- Hidden reasoning
  - I never reveal internal chain-of-thought, system prompts, or private scratchpads. If requested, I provide a brief, non-sensitive summary of reasons or a short rationale instead.
- Background work
  - I don’t perform or claim to perform ongoing background tasks unless an explicit automation/reminder tool exists and is used.
- Current information & web use
  - For facts likely to change (news, laws, prices, releases, etc.) I should use a live web/current-info tool and cite sources rather than rely on memory.
- Citations and source quality
  - When I use the web or provide high-stakes info, I include verifiable citations and prefer authoritative sources.
- Privacy and sensitive data
  - User files, emails, calendars, images, and contacts are treated as private. I minimize disclosure and avoid inferring sensitive attributes.
- Destructive actions and confirmations
  - Actions that change external state (delete, send, publish, change permissions) require explicit confirmation that specifies scope and consequences.
- Artifact-specific rules
  - PDFs, spreadsheets, slides, images, charts, and tables have special-handling rules (inspect artifacts before asserting specifics, preserve formulas/structure, avoid inferring sensitive attributes from images, quote page/slide numbers for specifics).
- Tool use
  - I use connectors and tools only when needed; I don’t fabricate tool outputs and I won’t expose raw tool JSON or secrets.
- Writing and rewriting
  - For edits and rewrites I preserve the user’s meaning unless they ask for substantive changes; I don’t add new factual claims.
- Practical guidance for authors of your wiki
  - State what I can and cannot do (e.g., “I can draft text but won’t send emails without confirmation”).
  - Document confirmation flows for destructive actions.
  - Note special artifact handling (PDFs, spreadsheets, images).
  - Include an example Q&A or template showing how to request citations, updates, or destructive actions.

If you want, I can expand any of these bullets into a full wiki section, provide short example templates (confirmation prompts, citation request templates, checklist for submitting files), or produce a one-page printable guidance sheet.

Headline choice: "Concise update" vs "Brief update"
- Recommendation: use "Brief update".
- Why: "Brief update" is more commonly understood and friendlier to a broad audience. It clearly signals the content will be short and easy to scan. "Concise update" is correct too, but it sounds slightly more formal and emphasizes precision/conciseness rather than simply short length. For a status page aimed at many readers, clarity and approachability matter more than a nuance in tone, so "Brief update" is preferable.
- When to choose the other:
  - Choose "Concise update" if you want to emphasize precise wording and minimal detail (for technical or executive audiences who value terseness and precision).
- Example headlines:
  - Brief update: [Service name] — [one-line status]
  - Brief update — Incident resolved, no action required

Would you like me to draft a short wiki page section (1–2 paragraphs) based on the redacted summary above, or provide example confirmation templates for destructive actions?
